question:
A 2-year-old boy presents with a swollen face and irritability. The patient's mother reports his urine was red this morning. 3 weeks ago, he presented to this same clinic with a ‘sandpaper’ rash and a red tongue with patchy hyperplastic fungiform papillae for which he was given broad-spectrum antibiotics. Laboratory tests reveal proteinuria, elevated antistreptolysin O, and decreased serum C3. Which of the following conditions mentioned below are triggered by a similar mechanism?
I. Arthus reaction
II. Myasthenia gravis
III. Acute rheumatic fever
IV. Polyarteritis nodosa
V. Rheumatoid arthritis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "2-year-old boy with swollen face and irritability" -> "red urine suggests hematuria" -> "recent history of 'sandpaper' rash and red tongue" -> "broad-spectrum antibiotics given" -> "laboratory tests show proteinuria" -> "elevated antistreptolysin O indicates recent streptococcal infection" -> "decreased serum C3 suggests complement consumption" -> "condition consistent with acute rheumatic fever" -> "acute rheumatic fever is an autoimmune response" -> "similar mechanism in Myasthenia gravis" -> "possible overlap with rheumatoid arthritis" -> 85%

CHAIN: "2-year-old boy with swollen face and irritability" -> "red urine indicates possible glomerulonephritis" -> "recent streptococcal infection indicated by elevated antistreptolysin O" -> "decreased serum C3 suggests complement activation" -> "acute rheumatic fever is a post-streptococcal complication" -> "Arthus reaction is a type III hypersensitivity" -> "Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder" -> "Polyarteritis nodosa is a systemic vasculitis" -> "Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune condition" -> "acute rheumatic fever shares mechanism with rheumatoid arthritis" -> 80%

CHAIN: "2-year-old boy with swollen face and irritability" -> "red urine suggests hematuria" -> "recent history of 'sandpaper' rash and red tongue" -> "broad-spectrum antibiotics given" -> "laboratory tests show proteinuria" -> "elevated antistreptolysin O indicates recent streptococcal infection" -> "decreased serum C3 suggests complement consumption" -> "condition consistent with acute rheumatic fever" -> "acute rheumatic fever is an autoimmune response" -> "Polyarteritis nodosa is also an autoimmune condition" -> "Arthus reaction is a localized immune complex reaction" -> "Myasthenia gravis is not triggered by similar mechanism" -> 75%

CHAIN: "2-year-old boy with swollen face and irritability" -> "red urine indicates possible glomerulonephritis" -> "recent streptococcal infection indicated by elevated antistreptolysin O" -> "decreased serum C3 suggests complement activation" -> "acute rheumatic fever is a post-streptococcal complication" -> "Arthus reaction is a type III hypersensitivity" -> "Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder" -> "Polyarteritis nodosa is a systemic vasculitis" -> "Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune condition" -> "acute rheumatic fever shares mechanism with rheumatoid arthritis" -> "unclear relationship with Arthus reaction" -> 70%
analysis: The clinical presentation suggests post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, which is associated with a previous streptococcal infection (indicated by elevated antistreptolysin O and decreased serum C3). Acute rheumatic fever (III) is also a post-streptococcal complication, triggered by a similar immune mechanism involving molecular mimicry. The other conditions listed (I, II, IV, V) do not share this specific post-infectious immune response mechanism. Therefore, the correct answer is option III, which is triggered by a similar mechanism as post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.
